headline: Historic House and Ferry Booking Advice
reservation: While the city is open, Fort Sumter ferry tickets and tours of historic mansions like the Nathaniel Russell House should be booked in advance to ensure preferred times. Major festivals in spring and fall can cause hotel shortages; check the official tourism board and NPS sites for seasonal event schedules and monument access.

days.title: Colonial History and Waterfronts

stops.name: Rainbow Row
stops.detail: Walk past the series of thirteen colorful historic houses to appreciate 18th-century architecture and local preservation.

stops.name: Waterfront Park
stops.detail: Visit the iconic Pineapple Fountain and take in views of the Cooper River and the Ravenel Bridge.

days.driving: Minimal; the historic district is best explored on foot. Conditions vary with city traffic.
days.note: Pavement can be uneven; comfortable walking shoes are necessary for the cobblestone streets.

days.title: Civil War Sites and Harbor Views

stops.name: Fort Sumter National Monument
stops.detail: Take the ferry to the island fort where the first shots of the Civil War were fired for a guided historical overview.

stops.name: USS Yorktown at Patriots Point
stops.detail: Explore the vintage aircraft carrier and maritime museum located just across the harbor in Mount Pleasant.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for the drive to Mount Pleasant; local ferry schedules are fixed.
days.note: Ferry departures are weather-dependent; check for cancellations during late summer storm seasons.

days.title: Lowcountry Nature and Ancient Oaks

stops.name: Angel Oak Tree
stops.detail: Marvel at this massive live oak, estimated to be several hundred years old, featuring sprawling, moss-draped branches.

stops.name: Folly Beach Pier
stops.detail: Conclude with a walk along the Atlantic coast to observe local surfing and search for shark teeth on the sand.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes to 1 hour for the loop; traffic on the Ashley River bridges can be heavy.
days.note: The Angel Oak site has specific closing times that differ from public parks; verify before arrival.

intel.title: Historic District Walking
intel.text: Many alleys and courtyards are pedestrian-only or have very restricted vehicle access. Use public parking garages on the perimeter of the French Quarter to avoid congestion.

intel.title: Mainland Supply Points
intel.text: Fuel stations are abundant in Mount Pleasant and North Charleston but scarce in the immediate historic peninsula. Fill up before heading to remote sites like the Angel Oak.

intel.title: City Market Congestion
intel.text: Street parking near the City Market is extremely limited and strictly enforced. Utilize the official parking decks on Meeting Street for easier access to the downtown core.

intel.title: Reliable Urban Coverage
intel.text: Cellular signal is strong throughout the city and nearby beaches. Expect slight drops in the more remote areas of the Francis Marion National Forest to the north.

intel.title: Midday Heat Strategy
intel.text: Summer humidity peaks between 12 PM and 4 PM. Plan indoor museum visits or shaded lunches during these hours to stay cool during the high season.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at Charleston International Airport and drive 22 minutes to the historic district; check-in at a boutique inn or hotel before exploring the Battery.
plan.vehicle: Compact cars are preferred for navigating narrow colonial streets and tight parking garages.
plan.goldenHour: The Battery seawall; ideal for viewing the harbor at sunset when the light hits the historic facades.
